'''Nayandeep Deka Baruah''' (born 1972) is an Indian [[mathematician]] and at present professor in the Department of Mathematical Sciences at [[Tezpur University]], India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tezu.ernet.in/dmaths/people/faculty.html|title=Faculty}}</ref> He is known for his work related to the mathematics of [[Ramanujan]], in particular he and his collaborators have found several Ramanujan type congruences using different methods.

== Biography ==

Baruah started his school education in Sibsagar district of Assam, and then went to [[Cotton College, Guwahati]], to do his bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1992. He graduated with a masters in mathematics from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] (IITK), India in 1995 and a [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from [[Tezpur University]], India in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web |title=faculty pages |url=http://www.tezu.ernet.in/dmaths/people/faculty-pages/ndb-web2016.pdf |website=www.tezu.ernet.in}}</ref> The title of his Ph.D. thesis was ''Contributions to Ramanujan's Schlafli-type Modular Equations, Class Invariants, Theta-functions, and Continued Fractions''.<ref>Mathematics Genealogy, [https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=174957 Nayandeep Deka Baruah]</ref> Following a short stint at [[Assam University]], [[Silchar]], Baruah has been a member of the faculty at Tezpur since 1997,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tezu.ernet.in/dmaths/people/faculty-pages/ndb.html|title = Faculty : Mathematical Sciences}}</ref> becoming full professor in 2009. For a period of one year in 2006–07, he was a visitor at the [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]] working with [[Bruce C. Berndt]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/ResearchAreas/numbertheory/ |title=Number Theory, Department of Mathematics, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign |access-date=2 June 2017 |archive-date=10 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170610093810/http://www.math.uiuc.edu/ResearchAreas/numbertheory/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

Baruah has been a recipient of the Young Scientist Award from the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 2004 and a BOYSCAST Fellowship from the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India in 2005–06.<ref>{{Cite web |title=faculty pages |url=http://www.tezu.ernet.in/dmaths/people/faculty-pages/ndb-web2016.pdf |website=www.tezu.ernet.in}}</ref>

== Professional contributions ==

Baruah has written over 50 research papers so far related to  [[special functions]], [[modular equation]], [[Basic hypergeometric series]] and [[integer partition]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nayandeep Deka Baruah |url=https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?hl=en&user=2U1ewzYAAAAJ&view_op=list_works |access-date=2024-05-04 |website=scholar.google.co.in}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=February 2024}} He has so far guided 14 students under him for their Ph.D. dissertation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=faculty pages |url=http://www.tezu.ernet.in/dmaths/people/faculty-pages/ndb-cv-web2024.pdf |website=www.tezu.ernet.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=174957|title = Nayandeep Baruah - the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> Baruah is also associated with giving several popular lectures for school and college students in different places of [[Assam]] as well as in other parts of the country; and is a member of the advisory board of the online magazine [[Gonit Sora]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gonitsora.com/about-us/|title=About Us}}</ref>

Baruah is a member of several distinguished professional societies and serves on several committees related to university education. He is also on the editorial board of the Journal of the Assam Academy of Mathematics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jaam.aamonline.org.in/ojs/index.php/j/about/editorialTeam|title=Editorial Team of Journal of the Assam Academy of Mathematics}}</ref> and the Journal of the [[Indian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.informaticsjournals.com/index.php/jims/pages/view/eb |access-date=2022-03-13 |website=www.informaticsjournals.com}}</ref>
